notes: The frame-derived screen index was used only to locate the decisive interval. No transcript or audio was used.

looked_at.what: The KL difference is visible above the chart while the compact second line is still being written; the p_2 add-on is green.
The compact line is fully readable as sum_i p_i log_2(p_i/q_i), and the add-on above the labels p_2 and q_2 is green.
The same fully readable compact KL line remains on screen, while the add-on at index 2 is now red.

steps.question: Which labelled add-on changes immediately after the compact KL sum becomes readable?
steps.why: At 1972.0 s the add-on aligned with p_2/q_2 is green; at 1973.0 s that same add-on is red.

steps.question: What is the observed colour transition?
steps.why: The pre- and post-transition frames at 1972.0 s and 1973.0 s show the two colours directly.

steps.question: How does one i-term reduce to the displayed logarithmic ratio?
steps.answer_text: p_i(-log_2 q_i) - p_i(-log_2 p_i) = p_i[-log_2 q_i + log_2 p_i] = p_i[log_2 p_i - log_2 q_i] = p_i log_2(p_i/q_i)
steps.why: The first difference and the compact sum are both visible at 1972.0 s; applying log a - log b = log(a/b) fixes the numerator as p_i.

answer: The changing add-on is at index 2 (the p_2/q_2-labelled bar), and it changes from green to red. Expanding one term gives p_i(-log_2 q_i) - p_i(-log_2 p_i) = p_i[-log_2 q_i + log_2 p_i] = p_i[log_2 p_i - log_2 q_i] = p_i log_2(p_i/q_i). Thus the displayed ratio is p_i/q_i; q_i/p_i would come from the opposite subtraction order.
basis: Frames t001972.jpg and t001973.jpg directly show the fully readable compact KL sum and the green-to-red transition at index 2; the log quotient identity is general knowledge applied to the displayed difference.
